title: Ticketing Platform: E2E QA Automation
subtitle: Playwright E2E tests, Pest integration tests, and Superset dashboards — eliminating manual regression, improving stability and scalability
seoTitle: Building E2E QA Automation for a Ticketing Platform
seoDescription: Architect and owner of Playwright E2E suite for checkout flows with 3 payment gateways, plus Pest integration tests and Superset embedding.
results: Comprehensive E2E test suite covering critical checkout flows
600+ backend integration test cases across critical flows
3 browsers covered (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)
3 payment gateways end-to-end tested including 3D Secure
Roughly 15–20 hours of manual regression per release replaced
body:
The Challenge

A white-label ticketing and event management platform (Laravel monolith since 2017) handling high-volume checkout flows across Spain and Latin America. Revenue flows — event creation, ticket delivery, payments through 3 gateways — had no end-to-end test coverage. Releases relied entirely on manual regression.

  • No existing E2E test suite; manual testing was unsustainable
  • Critical flows (checkout, discount codes, ticket resend via email/WhatsApp) lacked automation
  • Multiple payment gateways including 3D Secure flows were untested
  • Business stakeholders lacked real-time visibility into platform performance

What I Built

Playwright E2E Test Suite

Designed the entire testing strategy from scratch as owner of the E2E suite. Built a comprehensive Playwright + TypeScript suite that runs after every deploy to sandbox and staging: a critical gate of @critical tests first, then full coverage on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Tested checkout end-to-end with all 3 payment gateways including 3D Secure flows. Seeded test users instead of relying on email registration to ensure deterministic, fast tests.

Pest Integration Tests

Wrote robust integration tests covering API endpoints and critical business logic: /check, /resend, /me, /sessions endpoints; role-based permission checks (seller, admin, whitebrand); discount code validation and coupon management.

Superset Fork & Embedding

Introduced Apache Superset (fork) inside Docker; integrated Google OAuth and token-based secure embedding in Laravel with per-organizer row-level filtering. Enabled real-time dashboards on ticket sales, session activity, and user behavior.

Test Observability & CI/CD

Built an internal metrics tool (Node, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Chart.js) to track flaky tests and test duration per commit. Improved GitLab CI pipelines; standardized PR templates and internal documentation.

Stack

Laravel 12, PHP 8.4, Playwright, TypeScript, Pest, React 19, Apache Superset, GitLab CI, PostgreSQL.

title: WordPress E-Commerce — Amedia Social
subtitle: Resolved critical WooCommerce issues: cart calculation bugs and payment error messaging for a social media services platform
seoTitle: Fixing WooCommerce Cart & Payment Error Messaging
seoDescription: Debugged and fixed critical WooCommerce cart calculation bug caused by plugin updates, plus improved payment error messaging for better UX.
results: Cart calculations restored to accuracy
Payment error messages clarified for users
Checkout abandonment reduced
body:
Amedia Social, managed by Simbiotic Digital, approached me with two critical issues affecting their WooCommerce-based platform designed to boost social media performance and online reputation.

Issue 1 — Cart Calculation Bug

Users were experiencing incorrect total calculations whenever they selected product variations. After diving into the codebase, I discovered the problem stemmed from a JavaScript script responsible for dynamically calculating cart totals. A recent WooCommerce plugin update had altered the DOM structure of the cart page, leaving the script outdated.

By analyzing the new DOM structure and rewriting the script accordingly, I restored accurate pricing calculations, ensuring that users could confidently proceed with their purchases.

Issue 2 — Payment Error Messaging

When customers attempted to pay and the transaction failed, the error messages were vague and unhelpful, leading to frustration and abandonment. I implemented a solution using WooCommerce's woocommerce_add_error hook, creating a function to replace default messages with more descriptive, user-friendly explanations.

Outcome

Accurate cart calculations restored trust in the shopping experience, while clearer error messaging contributed to smoother customer interactions and reduced abandonment on the checkout page.

title: Real Estate Platform — Listing Los Cabos: From Inherited to Profitable

seoDescription: Took over a half-built portal, added Stripe subscriptions and security, serving Los Cabos and Mexico City. Now live with agent property management.
results: 2 cities/brands (Los Cabos, Mexico City) from one codebase
3 paid subscription plans (10/30/50 listings) with 60-day free trial
~10 agents managing their listings on the platform
From paper and Excel to live portal with full property visibility and development promotion

testimonial.quote: Juan took our real estate project from an idea to production. He delivered ownership, control, and a platform that works. We're live, profitable, and expanding.
testimonial.author: Julio César Pérez

body:
The Situation

A real estate portal for Los Cabos and Mexico City — half-built by previous developers in 2023, no unified property view, one person held all knowledge, property promotion was manual. The client lacked ownership of code and hosting.

The Challenge

  • Inherited codebase with incomplete features and no test coverage
  • No integration with Google Maps; property creation broken
  • Manual property promotion and activation
  • No subscription model or payment processing
  • Security issues: hardcoded keys, unvalidated Firebase access
  • Client unable to scale to a second city without external help

What I Built

Search & Discovery

Built a searchable property listing with filters (price, bedrooms, amenities) and an interactive Google Maps view. Integrated Google Maps for address autocomplete and geocoding.

Property Management

Property creation and editing workflows with image/video upload to Firebase Storage, status tracking (draft/active/sold), and agent profile assignment. Responsive design across devices.

Stripe Subscription System

Integrated Stripe payments end-to-end: checkout flow, webhooks for subscription lifecycle (creation, renewal, cancellation), plan limits (10/30/50 active listings per tier), 60-day free trial, discount codes. Each subscription tier unlocks different capabilities.

Security & Backend

Replaced hardcoded Firebase keys with environment variables. Added Firebase token validation on Node.js Express serverless backend (Vercel). Implemented reCAPTCHA on contact forms.

Multi-Brand Setup

Architected one codebase serving two cities: separate hero images, branding, and agent pools. Staging and production on Vercel with automated GitHub deployments.

External Security Review

Commissioned a professional security audit before scaling to the second city, ensuring platform readiness.

Stack

React 18, Tailwind CSS, Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage), Node.js/Express (Vercel Serverless), Stripe, Google Maps API.

title: Data Platform — Datakimia: Multi-Tenant BI SaaS
subtitle: Full-stack data platform with Next.js, NestJS, Superset embedded reports, per-customer isolation, and conversational AI agents
seoTitle: Building a Multi-Tenant BI SaaS with Embedded Superset
seoDescription: Founded NestJS backend (37 endpoints), executed Superset 4.1→6.1 migration in 30 days, built AI data agents over BigQuery with zero production impact.
results: 3 production customers isolated per deployment
Backend in production 2+ years without customer-facing outages
3 major Superset versions migrated in 30 days (Sep 8 – Oct 7)
Apache Superset fork with ~430 custom commits kept in sync with upstream
Superset 4.1 → 6.1 migration: 6 upstream merges, ~4,400 files in final merge, 23 automated wiring checks caught 3 silent regressions before production
5-phase / 17-step smoke test covering local → ephemeral → pilot → preprod → production
body:
The Challenge

Datakimia is a multi-tenant white-label analytics SaaS (US): each customer is isolated in its own deployment. The challenge: deliver embedded BI and conversational AI data agents securely per customer, and keep the BI layer (Apache Superset fork with ~430 custom commits) up to date without breaking production.

What I Built

NestJS Backend (37 Endpoints)

Founded and authored the production backend (first commit May 2024): Google/Microsoft Entra/Auth0 login, JWT tokens, role-based access control derived from Superset permissions, CASL-based authorization, per-customer data isolation. Production-grade for 2+ years without customer-facing downtime.

Superset Embedding & RBAC

Guest token generation for embedded dashboards with row-level security filters applied per customer. Dynamic dashboard filtering by customer context. Secure iframe embedding in the Next.js frontend.

Conversational AI Data Agents

Built chat-based data exploration over BigQuery using Google Gemini Data Analytics API (streaming SSE responses). Implemented voice agent with Gemini Live API for spoken data queries. Users ask questions in natural language; the agent translates to BigQuery SQL and returns insights.

Apache Superset 4.1 → 6.1 Migration

Migrated Datakimia's heavily customized Superset fork across 3 major versions (Sep 8 – Oct 7, 2024, ~30 calendar days). Process:

  • Inventory of ~430 custom commits classified into carry/replace/drop
  • 6 upstream merges with AI-assisted conflict resolution (Cursor) inside deterministic checks
  • Final merge touched ~4,400 files
  • 23 automated wiring checks; caught 3 features that had silently broken
  • 5-phase, 17-step smoke test (local → ephemeral → pilot → preprod → prod)
  • Effort: ~100 hours over 30 days

Stack

Next.js 14 (frontend), NestJS 10 (backend), Prisma ORM, PostgreSQL, Apache Superset, BigQuery, Google Gemini, GKE, Helm.

body:
For IVEE, a veterinary company dedicated to comprehensive animal care, I developed sophisticated scripts to streamline the extraction of vital medical information from PDF files containing canine patient medical histories.

Architecture

  • Google Storage bucket as the repository for PDFs uploaded by veterinarians
  • Cloud Function automatically triggered upon each file reception
  • The function reads and scrapes PDF contents based on the associated scraper for each system format
  • Modular design: new PDF formats accommodated by adding new scraping functions
  • Extracted data persisted in BigQuery for cross-department analysis
  • Interactive dashboards providing veterinarians insights into patient health and treatment history

The project spanned over a year and exemplified the dedication required to address complex challenges in veterinary healthcare through technology.
